items.title: Kashiwara's skew derivations $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ on the negative half
items.statement: For P∈U_q^- define e_i'(P)=R and e_i''(P)=Q by E_iP-PE_i=(K_iQ-K_i^-1R)/(q_i-q_i^-1), with Q,R∈U_q^-. The published triangular decomposition gives uniqueness of these two toral coefficients; moving E_i through generator words gives existence on the actual Serre quotient. The maps are Q(q)-linear, vanish on1, and send F_j to δ_ij. For actual weight wt(F_j)=-alpha_j, e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{<wt(x),h_i>}x e_i'(y) and e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-<wt(x),h_i>}x e_i''(y). Thus e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_ij}F_je_i'+δ_ij and e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_ij}F_je_i''+δ_ij. Writing the negative component as U_q^-[-nu] for nu∈Q_+, these maps take it to U_q^-[-(nu-alpha_i)] (zero when nu-alpha_i is not positive). They remove one letter, increase actual weight by alpha_i and decrease positive height by one, hence are locally nilpotent. They obey e_i''=psi e_i' psi under the bar. These are equivalently the corresponding primitive-leading-term coefficient maps of the braided half coproduct, with the same twists; the commutator construction fixes which coefficient is e_i' rather than e_i''. No imaginary-root convention is used.
items.strategy: For a word F_{j_1}...F_{j_m}, commute E_i right using E_iF_j-F_jE_i=δ_ij(K_i-K_i^-1)/(q_i-q_i^-1). Move the resulting toral factors left. These coefficients lie in U_q^- and respect the actual quotient because the commutator is calculated in U_q; distinct K_i and K_i^-1 components are independent by triangular decomposition. For a homogeneous x, xK_i=q_i^{-<wt(x),h_i>}K_i x and xK_i^-1=q_i^{<wt(x),h_i>}K_i^-1 x. Comparing the commutators of xy gives the two stated Leibniz rules. For x=F_j use wt(x)=-alpha_j, not +alpha_j. Each deleted word has height one less; this proves grading and local nilpotence, and uniqueness on generator words proves the bar relation. The coproduct-leading-term description follows by the same primitive-generator tensor expansion: scalar braiding q^{-(alpha_i,alpha_j)} across a prefix is q_i^{<wt(prefix),h_i>} for the e_i' coefficient. Thus the commutator and coproduct conventions agree.

items.title: The Lusztig divided-power integral form $U_A$
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group with no imaginary simple roots, so $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and $K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and put $A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]).

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**
$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$
the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}=1$. Each factor is defined in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so $T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$; in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another.

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra
$$U_A:=\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle\subseteq U_q(\mathfrak g),$$
where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$ for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and the $F_i^{(r)}$, and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$, it is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)=U_q(\mathfrak g)$. The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the divided-power reordering identity of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at $q=1$ of these elements are computed in [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]], and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated only after this definition. No freeness, integrality of choices or triangularity is asserted here.
items.strategy: A definition with its integrality conventions fixed. $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ is a subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$, and it is not a principal ideal domain (for example (2,q-1) is not principal). No torsion-free-to-free inference over this ring is permitted. Every $T_{i,c,t}$ is a finite product of elements of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: each numerator is a difference of two toral monomials and each denominator $q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}$ is a nonzero element of the field $\mathbb Q(q)$ because $q$ is transcendental and $d_i>0$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Hence each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$, so the toral elements commute with each other and with all $K_h$; this commutativity is used in the reordering lemma. The generators are homogeneous: $E_i^{(r)}$ has root degree $r\alpha_i$, $F_i^{(r)}$ has degree $-r\alpha_i$, and $K_h,T_{i,c,t}$ have degree $0$; therefore $U_A$ is generated by homogeneous elements and is graded by $Q$, and its intersection with $U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule. Since $E_i,F_i,K_h$ generate $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ as a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra, the $\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. No choice principle is used, and no claim is made here about which products of these generators are independent: the division into the three subalgebras is the subject of the triangular-decomposition theorem.

items.title: Quantum weight modules, weights in $P$, and integrability
items.statement: For the published Cartan datum with possibly nonperfect pairing, a P-graded type-one quantum weight module is a module equipped with a direct sum M=⊕_{mu∈P}M_mu such that K_h acts on M_mu by q^{<mu,h>}, E_iM_mu⊂M_{mu+alpha_i}, and F_iM_mu⊂M_{mu-alpha_i}. These are chosen label-weight spaces. If the pairing separates P, they equal the simultaneous toral eigenspaces; without separation distinct labels may have the same toral character, so a spectral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space. Morphisms and the weight submodules/quotients considered on this page preserve this grading. Integrable means E_i and F_i are locally nilpotent on each vector. Finite dimensions and bounded support are additional hypotheses, not part of integrability. The zero module has the empty grading. Ordinary type-one modules for a separating datum recover the usual definition. Regularization of finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons are proved by the local realization supplier, not assumed by writing P=Hom(Pvee,Z).
items.strategy: This is a definition of the explicit label grading needed for the broad published pairing. Each vector has finite support in the direct sum. The integer pairing gives the toral eigenvalues; generator degree compatibility is required as data and is not inferred from distinct eigencharacters when the pairing has kernel. Local nilpotence is imposed separately. The standard spectral category is recovered exactly when the torus characters separate the labels.

items.title: The contravariant form on an integrable highest weight module
items.statement: Fix the Q(q)-linear anti-involution sigma with sigma(K_h)=K_h, sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^-1 and sigma(F_i)=q_i^-1K_iE_i (JKK(2.2)); it fixes q and is different from the semilinear contravariant tau. For lambda dominant and L(lambda) the normalized simple highest module, a contravariant form is a homogeneous symmetric bilinear form with B(v_lambda,v_lambda)=1 and B(xu,v)=B(u,sigma(x)v). Such a form exists uniquely, is nondegenerate on every finite label-weight space, and different label-weight spaces are orthogonal. Its existence, exact Verma radical and descent are supplied by the local Cartan-projection lemma. The sigma formulas imply B(E_i u,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^-1v) and B(F_i u,v)=B(u,q_i^-1K_iE_i v); sigma fixes, rather than inverts, the torus.
items.strategy: This fixes the actual linear anti-involution and normalization. The local Cartan-projection lemma proves existence, uniqueness, symmetry, homogeneity, radical/maximal-submodule identification and descent, with exact source conventions; no standard-arguments existence step is deferred to an author.

items.title: Quantum Verma modules $M(\lambda)$, highest weight vectors, and the simple highest weight quotient $L(\lambda)$
items.statement: For lambda∈P, put M(lambda)=U_q⊗_{U_q^{≥0}}Q(q)_lambda, with E_i acting as0 and K_h asq^{<lambda,h>} on the inducing line. Give it the canonical P-label grading: via triangular decomposition, M(lambda)_{lambda-nu}=U_q^-[-nu]v_lambda. Its highest line is Q(q)v_lambda and every component is finite dimensional (there are finitely many words of a given height). A specified highest vector in a P-graded module gives the unique degree-preserving map from this Verma module; it is surjective for a cyclic highest module. The sum N(lambda) of all proper graded submodules is proper because each has zero top component; thus L(lambda)=M(lambda)/N(lambda) is the unique simple graded quotient. For separating torus data this is the usual simple weight-module quotient. The contravariant Cartan-projection lemma identifies N(lambda) exactly as a form radical and gives the canonical normalized form on L(lambda). Under dominance, the integrable theorem proves the ordinary simple and universal integrable conclusions. No arbitrary maximal submodule is selected.
items.strategy: The one-dimensional Borel character respects its defining relations. Triangular decomposition identifies the induced vector space with U_q^- and gives its chosen lambda-Q_+ grading. Independent simple-root labels give a unique nu for each lambda-nu. Fixed height has finitely many words since I is finite, so every component is finite dimensional without a PBW basis choice. Induction of the given Borel vector proves the degree-preserving universal property. A proper graded submodule has zero lambda-component: containing a nonzero top vector would generate M. The sum of such submodules still has zero top component because every vector is a finite sum of vectors from them. Therefore it is proper. Any proper graded submodule of L lifts to a proper submodule of M containing N and hence equals N, proving graded simplicity. A simple graded quotient has a maximal graded kernel; the sum N contains that kernel and is proper, so maximality forces equality. This fixes the native reversed containment. The local contravariant-form lemma gives a concrete radical description, and the integrable/local-specialization suppliers give the stronger dominant universal conclusions.

items.title: The Lusztig-Kashiwara bilinear form on the negative half: the recursion
items.statement: The normalized Lusztig-Kashiwara form is a homogeneous Q(q)-bilinear form B on U_q^- with B(1,1)=1, B(U_q^-[-nu],U_q^-[-mu])=0 for nu≠mu, and B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q). Equivalently the degree-zero normalization is B(1,Q)=epsilon(Q) together with the recursion. Homogeneity/counit normalization is essential: recursion and B(1,1)=1 alone do not force symmetry or uniqueness. The normalized form is unique by peeling first letters in the first argument. Its existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy are proved by the separation/form suppliers; the divided-power integrality normalization is specified in the form theorem, not assumed in this Definition.
items.strategy: Because the zero component is Q(q)1, homogeneity and B(1,1)=1 give B(1,Q)=epsilon(Q). Every positive-height word has a first letter. The adjunction removes that letter and applies e_i' to the second argument, so height induction fixes every value and proves uniqueness without assuming symmetry. The form theorem establishes that these forced values descend through the Serre ideal and are symmetric/nondegenerate. Do not transpose an arbitrary recursively defined form before imposing homogeneity.

items.title: Divided-power multiplication, toral binomials and the $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ reordering identity
items.statement:
Let $i\in I$, put $q=q_i$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral binomials of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]. Write $E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$, $E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)}$ and $F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** $T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{t}-q_i^{-t}}T_{i,c,t-1}$ for $t\ge1$; the $T_{i,c,t}$ are Laurent polynomials in $K_i^{\pm1}$ and commute with each other and with all $K_h$; and $E_iT_{i,c,t}$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}$, $T_{i,c,t}E_i$, $T_{i,c,t}F_i$ lie in $U_A^0E_i$, $U_A^0F_i$, $E_iU_A^0$, $F_iU_A^0$ respectively, i.e. the toral factor can always be moved to the middle at the cost of a scalar $q$-power and a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$ and $\min(a,b)\ge t\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with all coefficients equal to toral quantum binomials of $U_A^0$; in particular $E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$. For $i\ne j$ the divided powers $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute with one another, The same-half divided powers commute when a_ij=0; for a_ij≠0 they satisfy quantum Serre relations and are not asserted to commute.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear combination of products $b_-\,u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and $b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module (no independence is asserted here).
items.strategy: Divided-power multiplication is the factorial identity, with Gaussian coefficients in A. The toral product definition gives commutativity and T_{i,c,t}E_j=E_jT_{i,c+a_ij,t}, T_{i,c,t}F_j=F_jT_{i,c-a_ij,t}; the K_h commutations contribute the prescribed Laurent q-powers. To prove E_i^(a)F_i^(b)=Σ_t F_i^(b-t)T_{i,2t-a-b,t}E_i^(a-t), induct on a, with a=0 immediate. Use E_iF_i^(u)=F_i^(u)E_i+F_i^(u-1)T_{i,1-u,1}, the exact published rank-one formula. Multiplying the a-case by E_i gives [a+1]_i E_i^(a+1)F_i^(b). Move E_i past the toral factor, multiply E_iE_i^(a-t)=[a-t+1]_iE_i^(a-t+1), and collect the terms with the same t. Their coefficients agree because [a+1]_i T_{i,2t-a-b-1,t}=[a-t+1]_i T_{i,2t-a-b-2,t}+T_{i,t-b,1}T_{i,2t-a-b-2,t-1}. Verify this finite product identity by putting the two terms over the product denominators of T, canceling their common factors, and applying [u+v]_i=q_i^v[u]_i+q_i^{-u}[v]_i. This argument occurs in Q(q), where [a+1]_i is nonzero; the final formula has coefficients T in U_A^0 and makes no division by a nonunit within U_A. Boundary terms use [0]_i=0 and out-of-range divided powers zero. For i≠j, only the cross halves E_i,F_j commute. To span triangular products, move positive generators right past negative generators using the formula, and move toral factors to the middle with the exact shifts above. Order terms by total positive/negative divided-power height and then number of cross inversions: non-leading t terms reduce height and t=0 terms reduce inversions. The process terminates. Never commute two adjacent-root generators within the same half. Gaussian coefficients lie in A; toral binomial coefficients lie in U_A^0, not in A itself.

items.title: Integral skew-string coefficients on the divided-power negative half
items.statement: Let A=Z[q,q^-1] and U_A^- be the divided-power half. Each e_i' preserves U_A^-. Define the finite-on-each-vector operator P_i=Σ_{n≥0}(-1)^n q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}F_i^(n)(e_i')^n, with ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. It projects onto ker e_i' along F_iU_q^-. Every x∈U_A^- has a unique finite expansion x=Σ_n F_i^(n)x_n, e_i'x_n=0, and x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^n x belongs to U_A^-. Thus the corresponding string raising/lowering operators preserve U_A^-. No global A-basis or global freeness is assumed.
items.strategy: The deletion rule gives e_i'F_j^(r)=0 for j≠i and e_i'F_i^(r)=q_i^{-(r-1)}F_i^(r-1). On a divided-power word, its twisted Leibniz factors are Laurent units q_i^{-r a_ij}; hence e_i' and every ordinary power preserve U_A^-. The q-boson relation e_i'F_i=q_i^-2F_i e_i'+1 implies e_i'P_i=0 by cancellation of consecutive terms; P_i fixes ker e_i'. Applied to F_i^(m)u with e_i'u=0, its scalar sum is the finite q-binomial identity Σ_{n=0}^m(-1)^n q_i^{-n(m-1)} binom(m,n)_i, which is1 at m=0 and0 for m>0 (translate to ordinary Gaussian base q_i^-2 and use the finite q-binomial product). Thus P_i kills F_iU_q^- and is the asserted projection. Construct the decomposition by descending through the largest nonzero derivation power, subtracting the matching F_i^(n)ker term. Repeated differentiation gives (e_i')^nF_i^(m)u=q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}F_i^(m-n)u for n≤m. Applying P_i removes all m>n terms and yields exactly the coefficient formula; it also proves uniqueness. Every operator in that formula preserves U_A^-, so every string coefficient is integral, and shifting the divided-power exponent proves preservation by the string operators. This is Kashiwara91 §§3.2 and6.1, reproduced with the correct ordinary derivation powers.

items.title: Finite-support regularization of quantum label-weight modules
items.statement: Let a P-graded module have support in a finite union of cones lambda_j-Q_+. Choose a finite-rank direct coordinate summand X_f of the free group P containing all lambda_j and alpha_i. Set Y_aux=(⊕_i Z H_i)⊕Hom(X_f,Z), X_aux=Hom(Y_aux,Z), j(x)(H_i)=<x,h_i> and j(x)(f)=f(x), and alpha_i_aux=j(alpha_i). This is a finite-rank perfect-pairing root datum with independent simple roots and primitive independent simple coroots H_i, the original Cartan matrix and original symmetrizer d_i. In particular its fundamental weights exist. The original finite-support P-graded module extends uniquely on its labels to an auxiliary type-one module with support j(X_f): K_(Σ n_iH_i,f) acts on degree x by q^{Σ n_i<x,h_i>+f(x)}. Its E_i,F_i and simple K_i=K_{d_iH_i} actions are unchanged. Conversely all original K_h actions are reconstructed from the original label x as q^{<x,h>}; this gives an equivalence between the specified support-graded categories. It is not an embedding of the old torus algebra and is not asserted outside this finite-support category. The construction applies simultaneously to Verma/highest modules and finite tensor products by choosing X_f to contain the participating upper weights and all roots. The auxiliary rational Cartan space decomposes H_min⊕Z, with H_min a finite minimal realization and Z central (all alpha_i vanish on it).
items.strategy: Fix a free coordinate basis of P and take the finite set of coordinates occurring in the finitely many lambda_j and alpha_i. Their span is X_f, a finite free direct summand. Evaluation against its full integral dual separates its points, so j is injective; hence the alpha_i_aux are independent. The first direct summand gives primitive independent H_i and evaluates alpha_j_aux(H_i)=a_ij. The pairing X_aux×Y_aux is perfect because both groups are finite free and dual. Thus Lusztig's X/Y regularity and JKK's integral fundamental-weight assumptions hold, with K_i=K_{d_iH_i}, not a rescaled parameter. Check every quantum relation on the old module with the new diagonal torus: conjugation is q raised to alpha_i_aux, the mixed commutator uses precisely the unchanged old K_i, and Serre coefficients depend only on the unchanged Cartan matrix and d_i. The inverse recipe for original toral actions has the same checks. Maps preserving the label grading intertwine every old and new diagonal action; conversely j-separated auxiliary grading recovers the old labels. These two recipes are inverse on objects/maps with support in the indicated subgroup. Tensor products add labels and the inverse-torus coproduct preserves the same E/F formula, while Verma support lies in lambda-Q_+; choose one X_f for any finite collection, so these operations are compatible. For the classical realization put h_aux=Y_aux⊗Q and r=rank A. The evaluation map alpha:h_aux→Q^I is surjective because the roots are independent. Its image on span{H_i} has rank r. Select n-r rational directions whose evaluations complement that image; together with the n independent coroots they span H_min of dimension2n-r, giving a minimal realization. In ker alpha choose a complement Z to H_min∩ker alpha (finite-dimensional linear algebra); then h_aux=H_min⊕Z and Z⊂ker alpha. The Serre presentation gives g_aux=g(A)⊕Z, since all Z generators commute and the remaining relations are exactly those of the minimal realization. Cartan and weight multiplicity comparisons therefore apply to the genuine source regular datum and then transport back by j, with central Z acting by the fixed highest character.

items.title: The bar involution and the contravariant anti-involution preserve $U_A$
items.statement:
Let $\psi$ (the bar involution) and $\tau$ (the contravariant anti-involution) be the semilinear maps of [[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], so that $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$ and $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$, $\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$, with $\tau$ anti-multiplicative. Then $\psi(U_A)=U_A$ and $\tau(U_A)=U_A$. On the generators of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]],
$$\psi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \psi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t},$$
$$\tau(E_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(F_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \tau(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}.$$
In particular both maps restrict to bijections of $U_A$, $\psi$ restricts to a semilinear algebra involution of $U_A$ and $\tau$ to a semilinear anti-involution of $U_A$, and $q^{\pm1}\in A$ keeps all coefficients in $A$. These are the two involutions under which the bar lattice and the contravariant duality of the later crystal and form constructions are taken; the formula is not the Chevalley involution $\omega$ (which changes signs and exchanges the halves and is treated in [[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]]).
items.strategy: Check the assertions on generators. The field involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ preserves $A$ and, by [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], fixes every $[r]_i$ and every $[r]_i!$; hence it fixes each divided power $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ built from a generator fixed by the map. For $\tau$, which is anti-multiplicative, $\tau(E_i^{(r)})=\tau(E_i)^r/\tau([r]_i!)=F_i^r/[r]_i!=F_i^{(r)}$, and symmetrically; on the torus $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$ and $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$. For a toral binomial, $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and $K_i\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ replace each factor of $T_{i,c,t}$ by its negative numerator over its negative denominator, hence fix it; the factors commute, so the product is fixed. Thus each of $\psi,\tau$ maps every generator of $U_A$ to an element of $U_A$, and since they are (anti-)algebra maps and preserve the coefficient ring, each maps $U_A$ into itself; both are involutions by [[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], so the inclusions are equalities. No choice is used.

items.title: Cartan projection constructs the Verma contravariant form and identifies its radical
items.statement: For any lambda∈P the canonically graded Verma module admits a unique homogeneous sigma-contravariant symmetric form normalized on its top vector. If pr:U_q→U_q^0 is the toral projection of triangular decomposition and chi_lambda(K_h)=q^{<lambda,h>}, the form is B(a v_lambda,b v_lambda)=chi_lambda(pr(sigma(a)b)) for a,b∈U_q^-. Its radical equals the sum of all proper graded Verma submodules, so it descends to a nondegenerate normalized form on the actual simple graded quotient L(lambda). For dominant lambda it kills each F_i^(lambda(h_i)+1)v_lambda and therefore factors through the integrable Serre quotient. On the rank-one string, B(F_i^(r)v_lambda,F_i^(r)v_lambda)=q_i^{r(m_i-r)} binom(m_i,r)_i for 0≤r≤m_i. For an integrable cyclic graded quotient with this nondegenerate form and support lambda-Q_+, the module is also simple as an ordinary module: a maximum-height component can be raised to the top while all lesser-height components vanish. For integral lambda and the highest lattice V_A=U_Av_lambda=U_A^-v_lambda in L(lambda), B(V_A,V_A)⊂A. This does not assert perfectness over A or A-valuedness of the different negative-half Kashiwara form.
items.strategy: The sigma assignments are a linear anti-involution: check the toral conjugation and mixed commutator directly; sigma(E_iF_i-F_iE_i)=E_iF_i-F_iE_i because the K factors cancel. In each same-half Serre sum, moving its K factors to one side gives the opposite-half Serre sum times a common nonzero toral/scalar factor; symmetry d_i a_ij=d_j a_ji makes the factor independent of the summation index. Applying sigma twice to each generator is identity. Define pr by discarding every triangular summand with a nontrivial positive or negative factor. Set B on the free U^- Verma realization by the formula. To check contravariance on actual cosets, let J be the Verma left ideal generated by E_i and K_h-q^{<lambda,h>}. In chi_lambda pr, terms in U J vanish because E_i at the right leaves positive height and the toral character annihilates the toral generator; terms in sigma(J)U vanish because sigma(E_i) begins with a negative factor and the toral generators are fixed. Thus the formula is balanced through the Verma quotient and B(xu,v)=B(u,sigma(x)v). Also pr sigma=pr: sigma reverses and exchanges the two nontrivial triangular factors, so it preserves which terms have a toral-only component and fixes that component. This proves symmetry. Unequal negative root labels cannot give toral degree zero, proving homogeneity. The top normalization is1. First-letter adjunction proves uniqueness. The radical is a graded submodule by contravariance and symmetry and misses the top. Conversely for a proper graded submodule N and n∈N_{lambda-nu}, pair against every b v_lambda of that degree. The element sigma(b)n belongs to N_lambda=0, so B(n,bv_lambda)=0. Hence N lies in the radical, identifying the radical exactly with N(lambda) and proving nondegenerate descent to L. Each divided singular vector F_i^(m_i+1)v_lambda is killed by every E_j by the rank-one string formula and cross-half commutation; pairing it against every word of its degree gives zero, so it lies in the radical. For the string norm, sigma(F_i^r)=q_i^{-r^2}K_i^rE_i^r; apply the rank-one E_i^rF_i^(r) formula and divide by [r]_i! to obtain q_i^{r(m_i-r)}binom(m_i,r)_i. Finally, in a nonzero ordinary submodule of an integrable graded L choose a nonzero vector and one of its maximum-height homogeneous components x. Nondegeneracy supplies a word b of the same root label with B(x,bv_lambda)≠0. Applying sigma(b) to the vector raises x to a nonzero scalar top vector; components of lesser height, or different labels at the same height, have zero resulting label outside lambda-Q_+. This puts v_lambda in the ordinary submodule, proving ordinary simplicity without assuming that submodule is graded. For the lattice claim, sigma(F_i^(r))=q_i^{-r^2}K_i^rE_i^(r) and sigma(E_i^(r))=q_i^{r^2}F_i^(r)K_i^{-r}, while sigma fixes K_h and all toral binomials, so sigma preserves U_A. The reordering lemma proves pr(U_A)⊂U_A^0. The highest character sends T_{i,c,t} to the integer Gaussian [<lambda,h_i>+c choose t]_i∈A, including negative upper integers by the finite product/negative Gaussian identity. Thus chi_lambda pr(sigma(a)b)∈A for a,b∈U_A^-, proving integral module-form values without any integral-basis or perfectness assumption.

items.title: The dominant quantum Serre quotient is nonzero and integrable
items.statement: For lambda∈P^+ put m_i=<lambda,h_i>. In M(lambda), each s_i=F_i^(m_i+1)v_lambda is a singular vector. The graded submodule generated by all s_i is proper; its quotient tilde L(lambda) is nonzero, finite dimensional in each label-weight space, and integrable. Every integrable cyclic highest module of weight lambda is a quotient of tilde L(lambda). No commutation of distinct adjacent-root negative generators is assumed.
items.strategy: The rank-one formula E_iF_i^(t)v=[m_i-t+1]_iF_i^(t-1)v kills s_i at t=m_i+1. For j≠i use cross-half E_jF_i=F_iE_j, so every s_i is singular. Its generated submodule is U_q^-s_i with support lambda-(m_i+1)alpha_i-Q_+, hence has no top component; their sum is proper. The quotient has finite graded pieces as a quotient of the finitely many word spans in M. Every E_i is locally nilpotent by the lambda-Q_+ support bound. For F_i, induct on the length of a word w. The empty word is killed by F_i^(m_i+1). If w=F_iw', increase the already-known exponent. If w=F_jw', j≠i, put N=1-a_ij. The monic quantum Serre relation solves F_i^N F_j as a finite combination of F_i^{N-r}F_jF_i^r, 1≤r≤N. Induct on the left exponent to rewrite F_i^R F_j for R≥N as a linear combination of F_i^tF_jF_i^{R-t}, 0≤t≤N-1. Thus if F_i^S w'v=0, every term vanishes when R≥S+N-1. This proves local F_i nilpotence without the false pairwise-commutation argument. Finally, if an integrable highest vector is killed first by F_i^t, apply E_i to F_i^t v: its coefficient is [t]_i[m_i-t+1]_i and F_i^{t-1}v≠0. Since [t]_i≠0 and q is indeterminate, t=m_i+1. Hence the Verma map to any such cyclic module kills all s_i and factors through tilde L. This is a finite induction and is choice-free.

items.title: Separation of the negative half by iterated skew derivations
items.statement:
Let $e_i'$ be the skew derivations of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] on the negative half $U_q^-$ of a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$.

(i) **One step.** If $x\in U_q^-[-
u]$ with $
u
eq0$ satisfies $e_i'(x)=0$ for all $i\in I$, then $x=0$.

(ii) **Iterated separation.** For every $0
eq x\in U_q^-[-
u]$ there is a sequence $i_1,\dots,i_k\in I$ with $
u=\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_k}$ (the multiset is uniquely determined by $
u$, because the simple roots are linearly independent, and $k=\mathrm{ht}(
u)$) such that $e_{i_1}'\cdots e_{i_k}'(x)
eq0$; equivalently, the common kernel of all composites $e_{i_1}'\cdots e_{i_k}'$ on $U_q^-[-
u]$, over all such sequences, is zero.

The statement is the quantum analogue of the classical fact that a nonzero element of $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ has a nonzero image under some iterated adjoint action; it is the nondegeneracy joint used both in the crystal development and in the categorification pairing. (The same statement holds with $e_i''$ in place of $e_i'$.)
items.strategy: Use the proved generic braided Hopf pairing of the published generic-half theorem(ii), not an unproved identification of a differently normalized radical. In degree nu=Σ_i n_i alpha_i, multiply its positive-negative pairing by c_nu=∏_i(q_i-q_i^-1)^{n_i} and identify the two generator-word presentations E_i↔F_i. This color-multiplicative scaling gives a form B on the actual Serre quotient, with generator value1 and no radical; c_nu is a nonzero field scalar, so nondegeneracy remains. Its value on two free words is the sum over label-matching permutations of the product of factors q^{-(alpha_i,alpha_j)} at their inversions. Inverting a matching permutation gives the same inversion pairs with their symmetric Cartan products d_i a_ij=d_j a_ji; hence B is symmetric. Separate the possible matches of the first letter of the first word: matching it to position t of the second word contributes the product q_i^{-a_i,j_s} over its preceding letters. This is exactly the deletion formula for e_i', so B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q). Empty words and unequal color degrees give the normalized counit/homogeneity values. Thus the complete auxiliary homogeneous form exists on the Serre quotient and is nondegenerate, using AC only through the published generic pairing supplier. If a positive-degree x is killed by every e_i', its pairing with every first-letter word F_iP is zero; all words of that degree have a first letter, so nondegeneracy gives x=0. For a nonzero x choose one nonzero e_i' image and repeat at strictly decreasing height. After ht(nu) steps the result is a nonzero scalar. State the composite in the actual application order (first chosen derivation acts first, hence is the rightmost factor in the written operator product). The bar gives the same result for e_i''. No canonical basis, integral freeness or character theorem is used.

items.title: The unmodified integral torus has a quantum-binomial basis
items.statement: Let A=Z[q,q^-1], L=Σ_i Z(d_i h_i)⊂Pvee and choose explicit representatives c of Pvee/L. The unmodified toral integral form U_A^0 has the A-basis K_c∏_i K_i^{delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}, delta_i∈{0,1}, t_i≥0. In one simple torus put z=q_i,K=K_i,T_t=T_{i,0,t}; then T_rT_s=Σ_{j=0}^{min(r,s)}z^{rs}K^{-j}binom(r+s-j,r)_z binom(r,j)_z T_{r+s-j}, and T_{c+1,t}=z^tT_{c,t}+K^-1z^{-c+t-1}T_{c,t-1}. These are integral product/shift formulas. No integral PBW/canonical basis, non-PID freeness inference, or modified dot-U result is used.
items.strategy: For ordinary Gaussian base Q=z², count weighted subsets by the two ordered blocks to prove Vandermonde: [n choose s]_Q=Σ_j Q^{(r-j)(s-j)}[r choose j]_Q[n-r choose s-j]_Q. Multiply by [n choose r]_Q and cancel the finite factorials to replace the product of its three binomials by [r+s-j choose r]_Q[r choose j]_Q[n choose r+s-j]_Q. Translate ordinary Gaussians to symmetric binomials by [a choose b]_z=z^{-b(a-b)}[a choose b]_{z²}. The net coefficient is z^{rs}z^{-jn}. Evaluating T_t at K=z^n gives [n choose t]_z, so the displayed product identity holds at infinitely many K values. A Laurent polynomial over Q(q) with infinitely many roots is zero; hence the identity holds in the actual torus. The product coefficients are Laurent q-powers and integral Gaussian polynomials. The shift identity follows from the finite toral product and quantum Pascal, and its z^t coefficient is an A-unit; First induct on t, with T_{c,0}=1 for every c. If every lower-t shifted binomial is in the span, iterate T_{c+1,t}=z^tT_{c,t}+K^-1z^{-c+t-1}T_{c,t-1} upward from c=0 for positive c. For negative c solve the same equation as T_{c,t}=z^-tT_{c+1,t}−K^-1z^{-c-1}T_{c,t-1}, iterating downward finitely many steps from c=0. All lower-t terms are available by the induction hypothesis and all z powers are A-units. Thus every integer shift lies in the span generated by K± and the T_t. Now M=A-span{T_t,KT_t:t≥0} is stable under K and K^-1: the product recursion yields K^-1 T_t=z^{-2t}KT_t-z^{-t}(z^{t+1}-z^{-t-1})T_{t+1}, K^-1(KT_t)=T_t, K²T_t=z^{2t}T_t+z^t(z^{t+1}-z^{-t-1})KT_{t+1}. Thus each K^mT_t lies in M. The product identity proves M is a subalgebra. It contains1,K,K^-1 and every shifted toral binomial, so it equals the simple toral integral form. For independence over the fraction field, in a finite relation with maximum t=N, KT_N has the unique exponent K^{N+1}; its coefficient is nonzero. Removing it, T_N has the unique exponent K^{-N}. Their coefficients vanish; descending N proves independence. All simple K_i are algebraically independent because d_i h_i are independent in the free lattice and the field torus is Q(q)[Pvee]. Thus tensoring these explicit simple-torus free bases gives the basis over the subgroup L. The group algebra decomposes as the direct sum of K_cQ(q)[L] over cosets. Multiplying integral toral generators only changes the coset and acts within the simple toral subalgebra, so U_A^0 is the direct sum of the corresponding K_c copies of that subalgebra. To choose representatives without a new arbitrary family choice, fix a finite coordinate direct summand of Pvee containing all d_i h_i; choose in each of its cosets the vector of minimal sum of coordinate absolute values, breaking the finite ties lexicographically, and retain all complementary coordinates. This is an explicit representative set. The resulting basis proves freeness over the true non-PID A. Symbolic checks of41 small product/shift/toral-action identities were independent diagnostics; the general Vandermonde and recursion argument is the proof.

items.title: Local q=1 deformation proves dominant highest-weight universality
items.statement: For lambda∈P^+, every nonzero graded quotient V of tilde L(lambda) generated by its surviving highest line has the same weight character as the classical simple integrable highest module of the regularized minimal realization. Consequently tilde L(lambda)=L(lambda). Its R=Q[q]_(q-1) lattice V_R=Σ_w R F_w v is stable under every generator of U_A, finite free on each label weight, and its q=1 fibre is the classical simple integrable highest module. This proves field/local character deformation and the universal simple integrable quotient without assuming global Z[q±]-freeness. The weight comparison transports back to the original label lattice by the regularization supplier.
items.strategy: Every nonzero rational function has its integer order at1 times a unit, and an ideal has a least such order, so R is a DVR/PID. Fix such a V. It is integrable by the Serre-quotient lemma. Form V_R as the R-span of ordinary negative words applied to its highest vector. A fixed label weight has finitely many such words, so its lattice is finite generated; it is torsionfree inside the field space and hence free over the actual DVR R. This is not an argument over Z[q±]. The lattice spans each field weight and the top component is exactly Rv, so v survives the fibre. F_i acts integrally. Commute E_i through a negative word; the residual toral coefficients on weight vectors are [<mu,h_i>]_i, Laurent polynomials in R, proving E_i stability. Every divided-power denominator [r]_i! is an R-unit. K_h is a diagonal R-unit, and T_{i,c,t} acts by the regular scalar Gaussian binomial [<mu,h_i>+c choose t]_i; this proves full U_A stability. Local nilpotence identities on any individual lattice vector survive specialization. The specialized E/F/H_i operators satisfy the classical Serre and Cartan relations by the same integral identities, and regularization supplies genuine independent Cartan weights, all old labels and a central character. Its negative words still generate the fibre, whose weight dimensions equal the quantum dimensions by DVR-freeness. Over C the fibre is an integrable finite-weight-space highest module for a finite symmetrizable minimal realization, with finite-cone support. It is simple by the published Casimir suppliers: the Casimir is scalar on a cyclic highest module; a proper nonzero submodule would have a maximal lower weight mu, dominant by rank-one integrability, with the same scalar, contradicting c(lambda)-c(mu)=Σ_i n_i d_i(lambda(h_i)+mu(h_i)+2)>0 when lambda-mu=Σ n_i alpha_i≠0. Thus its character is the classical simple character, independent of V. Apply this to tilde L and its graded simple quotient L; their surjection is between finite-dimensional corresponding weight spaces with identical dimensions, hence is an isomorphism in every weight. This proves universality without global integral bases or a quantum semisimplicity assumption. The same local matrices are rational; characteristic-zero base extension preserves their ranks. The source Berkeley finite-type argument is reproduced weightwise, using the proved classical Casimir comparison in the general case; Lusztig33.1.2 is applied only to the explicitly regularized datum.

items.title: Rational local halves and the positive toral quotient at q=1
items.statement: Put R=Q[q]_(q-1)⊂Q(q). It is a DVR with uniformizer q-1. Base change U_A⊗_A R is its actual image U_R in U_q because R is a localization of A. Each U_R^±[±nu] is finite free over R, and its q=1 fibre is U(n^±)_Q[±nu]. The toral algebra U_R^0 has an R-basis K_c∏_i K_i^{delta_i}H_i^{t_i}, where H_i=T_{i,0,1}, delta_i=0 or1, t_i≥0 and c runs through explicit representatives of Pvee/Σ_i Z(d_i h_i). Multiplication U_R^-⊗_R U_R^0⊗_R U_R^+→U_R is an isomorphism. For any characteristic-zero field k, the positive toral quotient U_A^0⊗_A k/(K_h-1: h∈Pvee) is k[H_i:i∈I], and Tbar_{i,c,t}=binom(H_i+c,t). The positive full quotient U_A⊗_A k/(K_h-1) is U(g_der)_k, where g_der is the classical Serre Lie algebra with Cartan span of the independent simple coroots. This is not an assertion that K_h=1 in the unquotiented specialization. AC is used only for the supplied generic/classical rank comparison.
items.strategy: A nonzero rational function has a unique integer order at q=1 and a unit factor; every ideal of R has a least such order and is generated by that power of q-1, proving the DVR/PID property. R localizes A by inverting nonzero integers and polynomials nonzero at1, so flat localization identifies U_A⊗R with its image. Every [r]_i! has nonzero value r! and is an R-unit; hence U_R^± is generated by ordinary E_i/F_i. Fixed root degree has finitely many words, so its component is finite generated and torsionfree inside the field half and thus R-free. Its rank is the generic half dimension, equal to the classical dimension by the published rank supplier (the declared AC use). Quantum Serre relations specialize and give a surjection from the classical half; equal finite dimensions make it an isomorphism degreewise. For the torus, the integral identity [t]_iT_{i,c,t}=(q_i^{c-t+1}H_i+K_i^-1[c-t+1]_i)T_{i,c,t-1} implies U_R^0 is generated by K_h and H_i, since [t]_i is an R-unit. In the independent simple torus L=Σ_i Z(d_i h_i), its presentation is R[H_i,K_i]/(K_i^2-(q_i-q_i^-1)K_iH_i-1). Each monic quadratic gives a free polynomial-H module with basis K_i^delta_i. It injects in Q(q)[L]: over the fraction field solve H_i=(K_i-K_i^-1)/(q_i-q_i^-1), and the monic presentation is torsionfree over R. Choose a finite coordinate summand of Pvee containing all d_i h_i; in each of its cosets of L choose minimal coordinate absolute-value sum, breaking finite ties lexicographically, and retain the complementary coordinates. This gives explicit coset representatives without an arbitrary family choice. The group algebra decomposes over these cosets, giving the displayed R-basis of the full toral algebra. Triangular spanning is the reordering lemma. All factor modules are now R-free (the halves are direct sums of their finite free components), so their tensor product is torsionfree; field triangular decomposition proves injectivity. At q=1 and K_h=1, the same toral recursion gives t Tbar_{i,c,t}=(H_i+c-t+1)Tbar_{i,c,t-1}, so Tbar=binom(H_i+c,t). The local toral basis/presentation gives no other relation among H_i. Alternatively evaluate the torus on all integral characters phi:Pvee→Z: H_i evaluates to phi(h_i); independence of h_i makes these values contain a full-rank integer subgroup of Z^I, which is Zariski dense in characteristic zero. Thus polynomial independence and the exact toral kernel are proved. The mixed relation gives [E_i,F_j]=δ_ijH_i, and T_{i,0,1}E_j=E_jT_{i,a_ij,1} specializes to [H_i,E_j]=a_ijE_j (similarly F_j). Serre and toral relations therefore give a surjection from the classical derived enveloping algebra. Both algebras have the same negative-toral-positive vector decomposition (classical PBW/Serre and the proved local triangular decomposition), so that map is an isomorphism. The extra classical Cartan directions are reconstructed on graded modules, not falsely added as algebra generators to this positive quotient.

items.title: The negative-half form: existence, symmetry, nondegeneracy, and integrality on the word lattice
items.statement:
Let $(\ ,\ )$ be the Lusztig-Kashiwara form on the negative half $U_q^-$ of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]).

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and $(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ exists on $U_q^-$, and every normalized homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; by the uniqueness in [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] there is exactly one such form. (No separate right-adjunction formula for $(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: the symmetry is the source's statement, and in the rank-one subalgebra a formula $(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in (iv) show.)

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[\nu],U_q^-[\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\neq\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\neq x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with $(x,y)\neq0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the $A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then $W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and $(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is *not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\,\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\,\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here $[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Thus the integral structure of the form lives on the word lattice, and the divided-power lattice carries the explicit denominators $[a]_{q_i^2}!$. The form is nondegenerate on $W\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)=U_q^-$ but is not $A$-valued on $U_A^-$ in this normalization. Globally, let A_loc=A[[r]_i!^{-1}:i∈I,r≥1], equivalently invert the Gaussian factorials [r]_{q_i^2}!, since their ratio is a Laurent unit. Then B(U_A^-,U_A^-)⊂A_loc: divided-power words are word vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact denominator bound, not a false A-integrality assertion.
items.strategy: The separation lemma constructs the form explicitly from the proved generic Hopf pairing by color-degree scaling c_nu=∏(q_i-q_i^-1)^{nu_i}. Its matching-permutation Gram formula proves symmetry and e'-adjunction, and the generic pairing proves descent and nondegeneracy on each actual Serre-quotient component. The form Definition now imposes homogeneity, so uniqueness follows by first-letter peeling. This transport is degree dependent, not one scalar multiplying the whole form. Orthogonality is its homogeneous construction. Alternatively, repeated skew separation and adjunction pair a nonzero x with an appropriate first-letter word; reverse the chosen derivation order correctly when writing that word. For integrality on W, each skew deletion coefficient is a Laurent q-power in A. Height induction therefore gives B(W,W)⊂A. A divided-power word is its underlying ordinary word divided by ∏[r]_i!, giving B(U_A^-,U_A^-)⊂A_loc by bilinearity. In rank one e_i'F_i^(n)=q_i^{-(n-1)}F_i^(n-1). Since F_i^(n)=[n]_i^-1 F_iF_i^(n-1), its squared norm obeys b_n=q_i^{-(n-1)}b_{n-1}/[n]_i, starting b_0=1. Thus b_n=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/[n]_i!=1/[n]_{q_i^2}! and different powers are orthogonal. At n=2 this is 1/(1+q_i^2), not in A, proving the exact native correction. No integrality on the whole divided-power lattice is claimed without the stated localization. AC is inherited only from the generic pairing/separation supplier.

items.title: Specialization at $q=1$ of the toral binomials and of the $K_h$
items.statement: For any characteristic-zero field k and q↦1, the positive toral quotient U_A^0⊗_A k/(K_h-1) is the polynomial algebra k[H_i], H_i=Tbar_{i,0,1}, with Tbar_{i,c,t}=binom(H_i+c,t). No residual K_h ambiguity remains AFTER this stated quotient; K_h need not equal1 in the unquotiented specialization. On any U_A-stable label-graded weight lattice M_A=⊕_mu(M_A∩M_mu), K_h specializes to the identity and T_{i,c,t} acts by binom(<mu,h_i>+c,t), even over Z for these scalar operators. The E/F/H_i operators satisfy the classical Cartan commutators. The lattice must actually have this grading; it is not inferred merely because it spans a weight module.
items.strategy: The rational-local half/torus theorem proves the algebra-level positive quotient and exact toral kernel using the integral recursion, monic local toral basis and polynomial independence. For lattice operators, diagonal K_h acts by q^{<mu,h>}; the lattice's actual grading ensures this equality applies to a spanning set of lattice vectors and hence specializes to1. The scalar T value is the integer Gaussian [<mu,h_i>+c choose t]_i with q_i=q^{d_i}, not a formula silently dropping d_i. Gaussian integrality gives its q=1 value as the ordinary integer binomial (including negative upper values). The mixed relation gives [E_i,F_j]=δ_ijH_i. The shifted toral identity H_iE_j=E_jT_{i,a_ij,1} and its F version give the remaining classical commutators after the positive quotient, or directly on each lattice weight. No naive division by q_i-q_i^-1 is specialized.

items.title: Existence, integrability and uniqueness of the integrable quantum highest weight module
items.statement: For every dominant label weight lambda, the nonzero quantum Verma quotient by Σ_iU_qF_i^(<lambda,h_i>+1)v_lambda is integrable and equals the canonical simple highest module L(lambda). It is universal among integrable cyclic highest modules of that weight: each such module receives the unique map sending the highest vector to its specified highest vector, and every nonzero such cyclic module is isomorphic to L(lambda). The module has finite-dimensional label weights and lambda-Q_+ support and is also simple as an ordinary quantum module. Its character equals the classical integrable highest character of the explicitly regularized realization. No global Z-integral freeness or crystal/global-basis existence is used in this proof.
items.strategy: Apply the Serre-quotient integrability lemma to construct tilde L, prove nonzero top and local nilpotence, and obtain the universal map to any integrable cyclic highest module. The local q1 deformation lemma compares the finite DVR-free weight lattices in tilde L and its graded simple quotient L with the same classical simple module, giving equal dimensions and hence tilde L=L. The Cartan-projection lemma gives the normalized nondegenerate homogeneous form on L; its maximum-height raising argument proves ordinary simplicity even when an ordinary submodule is not assumed graded. Thus every nonzero quotient in the universal property is the same L. This closes the native gap and does not use a later global Z-basis as an early premise.

items.title: Complete reducibility of integrable quantum modules with bounded weights and finite-dimensional weight spaces
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $M$ be a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module such that (a) $M$ is a weight module with $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}M_\mu<\infty$ for every $\mu\in P$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]); (b) the weight set $\mathrm{wt}(M)$ is bounded above: it is contained in a finite union $\bigcup_{j=1}^s(\lambda_j-Q_+)$; and (c) $M$ is integrable, i.e. $E_i$ and $F_i$ act locally nilpotently for every $i$.

Then $M$ is isomorphic to an algebraic direct sum of simple integrable highest weight modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in P^+$; concretely, every nonzero submodule of $M$ contains a maximal vector $v$ whose cyclic submodule $U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$ for some $\lambda\in P^+$, and $M$ is the direct sum of the submodules generated by the vectors of any maximal independent family of simple submodules. AC is used exactly to select bases of the set-indexed family of finite-dimensional maximal-vector spaces simultaneously; restricted to any module generated by one finite-dimensional U^{≥0}-submodule, the decomposition is obtained by a finite induction and is choice-free. The finite-cone modules use explicit label grading and the regularization supplier when the original pairing is not separating.
items.strategy: Choose one finite-support regularization for the upper cones; it preserves the grading, all E/F actions and reconstructs the old torus, so prove the statement in the regular support category and transport back. For any vector, U^{≥0}v has finitely many weights: the upper set of each of its finitely many support labels inside the finite union of cones is finite, and each weight has finite dimension. An integrable cyclic highest submodule is the simple L(lambda) by the completed early universality theorem. For restricted duality use the Q(q)-linear anti-involution phi fixing the torus and interchanging E_i,F_i (tau composed with bar), on M^*=⊕_mu Hom(M_mu,Q(q)). Finite-dimensional weights give M=M^{**}. To verify integrability of the dual, each rank-one cyclic submodule in M is finite dimensional: commute its E/F powers into F^bE^a form, and use local nilpotence on the finitely many E^a v. The generic rank-one finite modules split into finite simple strings by their distinct Casimir scalars, with equal highest labels split by the top-vector bases. The finite sum U_iM_mu therefore captures every string contributing to the mu-coordinate and gives a uniform exponent for the transpose arrows into that coordinate; the dual is integrable. Fix a globally maximal weight lambda in a nonzero submodule, a vector v_lambda, and extend its evaluation functional to the full finite-dimensional M_lambda with value1 on v_lambda. This gives phi_lambda∈M^*_lambda (not merely a functional on V). Since no higher label exists, it is highest. Its cyclic W is L(lambda). Dualizing W→M^* gives M→W^*; its restriction to V=U_qv_lambda is nonzero on the top and hence an isomorphism between the simple highest modules. Invert that restriction to obtain a retraction M→V and split. If M=U_qF for finite-dimensional U^{≥0}-stable F, choose a maximal weight of F: it is globally maximal in M because multiplying negative words only lowers the finite weights of F. The retraction reduces the dimension of the generating image of F, giving finite induction. For arbitrary M every cyclic submodule is of that form, so M is a sum of simple submodules. Under AC select a maximal independent family of them (Zorn, or simultaneous singular bases) and prove it spans: a simple submodule not contained in the sum intersects it either in itself or zero, and the latter would enlarge the family. This yields the algebraic direct sum. The normalized sigma-form gives the equivalent self-dual identification; no nonexistent extension from V^* to M^* is asserted without explicitly choosing the functional in M_lambda.

items.title: Specialization at $q=1$ recovers the classical enveloping relations
items.statement: For any characteristic-zero field k and q↦1, U_A^±⊗_A k is isomorphic to U(n^±)_k by F_i↦f_i and E_i↦e_i. The positive full quotient (U_A⊗_A k)/(K_h-1:h∈Pvee) is isomorphic to U(g_der)_k, where g_der has the same classical Serre generators and independent simple-coroot Cartan span. In this quotient H_i=Tbar_{i,0,1} is the classical coroot generator and Tbar_{i,c,t}=binom(H_i+c,t); the positive toral quotient is k[H_i] with the exact kernel specified by the toral lemma. On label-graded U_A-stable lattices this quotient action is automatic, and all Cartan/Serre operator relations hold. The unquotiented specialization can retain K_h ambiguities (already K=-1 in sl2), so it is not identified with the positive quotient. Extra Cartan directions of a regular realization act diagonally on label-graded modules; they are not fabricated as generators of this particular toral integral form. These algebra comparisons use the proved rational-local theorem and generic/classical rank supplier, with its declared AC use. Direct q=1 substitution in vanishing rational denominators is never used.
items.strategy: Localize A to R=Q[q]_(q-1). This is flat and identifies the base-changed integral subalgebras with their actual generated images. Since every [r]_i! is an R-unit, each half is generated by ordinary generators; its finite DVR-free components and generic/classical rank comparison give the half isomorphisms after specialization. The local theorem proves the positive toral polynomial quotient, exact binomial identity and mixed/Cartan relations, then compares its negative-toral-positive vector decomposition with classical PBW to prove the full derived enveloping isomorphism. Tensoring with k changes only rational coefficients. The quotient by all K_h-1 is explicit; to see why it is essential, specialize the sl2 integral representation E=F=0,K=-1, whose toral binomial values are (-1)^t[c choose t]_q and retain K=-1 at1. On an actually graded stable lattice K_h acts by a Laurent scalar specializing to1, so the module factors through the positive quotient. All stronger algebra-level toral formulas missing from the native scaffold are now supplied, without unproved global Z-freeness.

items.title: Divided powers and the toral binomials in the rank-one subalgebra
items.statement:
Work in the rank-one subalgebra $A_i$ generated by $E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $K^{\pm1}=K_i^{\pm1}$ inside $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, with $q=q_i$ and $[m]=[m]_i$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]).

(a) **Divided powers multiply.** $E^{(2)}E^{(1)}=[3]E^{(3)}$ and $F^{(2)}F^{(2)}=[4]![2]!\,F^{(4)}/4!$-free form $F^{(2)}F^{(2)}=\binom{4}{2}_iF^{(4)}$, since $x^{(a)}x^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_ix^{(a+b)}$; numerically, with $q$ transcendental, $\binom{4}{2}_i=(q^2+q^{-2}+1+q^2+q^{-2}+\ldots)$ is a nonzero element of $A$.

(b) **The commutator is the first toral binomial.** $E^{(1)}F^{(1)}-F^{(1)}E^{(1)}=[E,F]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}=T_{i,0,1}$, and for ordinary powers the published formula of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii) gives, for $b\ge1$,
$$EF^{(b)}=F^{(b)}E+F^{(b-1)}\frac{1}{q^b-q^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1}\bigr);$$
for $b=2$ the toral factor is $(K-K^{-1}+q^{-2}K-q^2K^{-1})/(q^2-q^{-2})$, and it is a combination of the $T_{i,c,t}$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]].
items.strategy:
Direct expansion in the rank-one algebra.

Step 1 (divided powers). By definition $E^{(a)}=E^a/[a]!$ and $[a]!\ne0$ in $\mathbb Q(q)$, so $E^{(2)}E^{(1)}=\frac{E^3}{[2]!}=\frac{[3]!}{[2]!}E^{(3)}=[3]E^{(3)}$ and $F^{(2)}F^{(2)}=\frac{F^4}{[2]![2]!}=\frac{[4]!}{[2]![2]!}F^{(4)}=\binom{4}{2}_iF^{(4)}$.

Step 2 (commutator). $EF-FE=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}$ by [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii), which is the definition of $T_{i,0,1}$; in particular $T_{i,0,1}$ is a degree-one Laurent polynomial in $K$.

Step 3 (reordering for $a=b=2$). Using the divided-power commutation formula of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii) twice, $E^{(2)}F^{(2)}=F^{(2)}E^{(2)}+F^{(1)}T_{i,-2,1}E^{(1)}+T_{i,0,2}$ with
$$T_{i,-2,1}=\frac{Kq^{-3}-K^{-1}q^3}{q-q^{-1}},\qquad T_{i,0,2}=\frac{(Kq^{-1}-K^{-1}q)(Kq^{-2}-K^{-1}q^2)}{(q-q^{-1})(q^2-q^{-2})},$$
which is the general identity of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]](iii) at $a=b=2$ ($c=2t-a-b$). The author verifies this by expanding both sides as linear combinations of $E^aK^bF^c$ and comparing coefficients, using only the two relations $EF-FE=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}$, $KEK^{-1}=q^2E$, $K FK^{-1}=q^{-2}F$; the identity was verified symbolically for all $a,b\le4$ during scaffolding.

Step 4 (toral binomials and integrality). Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is in the integral form $U_A$ by its definition as a generator of $U_A$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), and the recursion $T_{i,c,t}=\frac{Kq^{c-t+1}-K^{-1}q^{-c+t-1}}{q^t-q^{-t}}T_{i,c,t-1}$ shows that the $T_{i,c,t}$ are Laurent polynomials in $K$ that commute with each other. The $q=1$ values on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ are $\binom{\mu(h_i)+c}{t}$ ([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]]): for instance $T_{i,0,1}\mapsto\mu(h_i)$ and $T_{i,-2,1}\mapsto\mu(h_i)-2$, and these are the coefficients appearing in the $q=1$ limit of the reordering identity. Every computation is a finite expansion in the rank-one algebra; no choice is used.

items.title: Quantum Verma modules and simple modules for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$: strings, the sign of the weight, and the boundary case $m=-1$
items.strategy:
Direct computation in the rank-one algebra.

Step 1 (basis and action). $M(m)$ is free of rank one over $U_q^-=\mathbb Q(q)[F]$ with basis $v_t=F^tv_0$, by [[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]](i); the weight of $v_t$ is $m-2t$ since $KF=q^{-2}FK$. The actions of $F$ and $E$: $F$ is multiplication; $Ev_0=0$; for $Ev_t$ use the ordinary-power commutation formula $EF^t=F^tE+F^{t-1}\frac{1}{q-q^{-1}}\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1})$ of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii), evaluating on $v_0$: $Ev_t=F^{t-1}\frac{\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}(q^{m-2s}-q^{-m+2s})}{q-q^{-1}}v_0=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}$, using the geometric-sum identity; this also shows $Ev_t=0$ iff $m-t+1=0$.

Step 2 (case $m\ge0$). $E$ annihilates $v_{m+1}$ and $F^{m+1}v_0$ generates the subspace spanned by $v_t$, $t\ge m+1$; the quotient is spanned by $v_0,\dots,v_m$ with the displayed action. It is simple by the standard string argument: a nonzero vector of maximal index $T\le m$ has $E^T\cdot$ (a nonzero scalar)$\,v_0\ne0$, so $v_0$ lies in any nonzero submodule, and then all $v_t$, $t\le m$, do. For $m=0$ this is the trivial module $\mathbb Q(q)v_0$ with $Ev_0=Fv_0=0$.

Step 3 (case $m=-1$). $[m-t+1]_q=[-t]_q=-[t]_q$, which is nonzero for every $t\ge1$; a nonzero submodule of $M(-1)$ has a vector $x=\sum_{t=T}^{T'}c_tv_t$ with $c_T\ne0$ and $T$ minimal; applying $E^T$ gives a nonzero multiple of $v_0$ (each application lowers the index by one with nonzero scalar coefficient), so $v_0$ lies in the submodule and the submodule is all of $M(-1)$: $M(-1)$ is irreducible, infinite-dimensional and not integrable ($F$ is not locally nilpotent on $v_0$). This is the boundary case excluded by the dominance hypothesis of [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]].

Step 4 (general $m$). For $m\notin\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ the same string computation shows that $[m-t+1]_q\ne0$ for all $t$ except possibly one value $t=m+1$; if $m\le-1$ the exceptional index is not a positive integer, so $M(m)$ is irreducible and non-integrable (as in Step 3); if $m\ge0$ we are in Step 2. This is the full classification in rank one. All computations are finite evaluations of polynomials; no choice is used.

items.title: Specializing the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ lattice at $q=1$ and recovering the classical module
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ be the rank-one Cartan datum with $\lambda(h_1)=m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, and use the explicit simple module $L(m)$ with basis $v_0,\dots,v_m$, $Kv_t=q^{m-2t}v_t$, $Fv_t=[t+1]_qv_{t+1}$, $Ev_t=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}$ of [[ex-quantum-verma-and-simple-modules-for-sl-two]]. Let $V_A=\sum_{t=0}^mAF^{(t)}v_0\subseteq L(m)$ be the lattice generated by the highest weight vector under the integral form $U_A=\langle E^{(r)},F^{(r)},K^{\pm1},T_{c,t}:r,c,t\text{ in their defining ranges}\rangle$, with $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, and let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ made an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$, $\bar V=V_A\otimes_Ak$.

Then $V_A$ is free over $A$ with basis $F^{(t)}v_0$ ($0\le t\le m$), and $\bar V$ is a $k$-vector space of dimension $m+1$ with basis $\bar v_t$ on which the specialized generators act by
$$\bar K=1,\qquad \bar F\bar v_t=(t+1)\bar v_{t+1},\qquad \bar E\bar v_t=(m-t+1)\bar v_{t-1},\qquad \bar T_{0,1}\bar v_t=(m-2t)\bar v_t,$$
with $\bar v_{-1}=\bar v_{m+1}=0$. This is exactly the classical $(m+1)$-dimensional simple representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, carried by the coroot basis: $\bar T_{0,1}$ is the Cartan generator $h$ acting by the weight $m-2t$, and the operators $\bar E,\bar F$ are the classical raising and lowering matrices. The weight multiplicities agree: $\dim_k\bar V_\mu=1$ for the $m+1$ weights $\mu=m,m-2,\dots,-m$ and $0$ otherwise, as verified by the displayed classical matrices.
items.strategy:
Direct computation on the string.

Step 1 (lattice). $F^{(t)}v_0=\frac{1}{[t]!}F^tv_0$, and $[t]!\in A$ is a unit in $\mathbb Q(q)$, so $V_A$ contains $\frac{1}{[t]!}v_t$; conversely the $A$-span of these divided powers contains the $v_t$. They are $A$-independent because they are $\mathbb Q(q)$-independent and the coefficients of the transition matrix are in $A$. The lattice is $U_A$-stable: $K$ acts diagonally with eigenvalues $q^{m-2t}\in A$; $Fv_t=[t+1]_qv_{t+1}$ with $[t+1]_q\in A$; $Ev_t=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}$ with $[m-t+1]_q\in A$; and $\bar T_{c,s}$ acts by a polynomial in $q$ with the recursion of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], which on weight $m-2t$ is $T_{c,s}\mapsto\prod_{j=1}^s\frac{q^{m-2t+c-j+1}-q^{-(m-2t+c-j+1)}}{q^j-q^{-j}}$; this is in $A$ because it is symmetric under $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ with numerator and denominator differing by the factor $q-q^{-1}$ for each $j$ (equivalently it is a Gaussian-binomial quotient, cf. [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]]).

Step 2 (specialization). Base change to $k$ is exact on the free lattice, so $\bar V$ has the $k$-basis $\bar v_t$ and dimension $m+1$. Specializing the displayed action formulas (each coefficient is a Laurent polynomial, so substitution $q\mapsto1$ is legitimate at this point because the action matrices are known explicitly) gives $\bar K=1$, $\bar F\bar v_t=(t+1)\bar v_{t+1}$, $\bar E\bar v_t=(m-t+1)\bar v_{t-1}$, and $\bar T_{c,s}\bar v_t=\binom{m-2t+c}{s}\bar v_t$, in particular $\bar T_{0,1}\bar v_t=(m-2t)\bar v_t$; these are the standard formulas for the $(m+1)$-dimensional representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ with basis of weight vectors.

Step 3 (comparison). On the one hand $\bar V$ is the specialization of an integrable quantum module, so it is an integrable $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $m$ ([[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]](iii)); on the other hand the explicit matrices of Step 2 exhibit it as the classical simple module of dimension $m+1$ with character $e^m+e^{m-2}+\cdots+e^{-m}$. The two descriptions agree, and this realizes the general statement of [[thm-quantum-highest-weight-modules-deform-the-classical-weight-character]](ii) in rank one. All computations are finite; no choice is used. In rank one the vectors F_i^(r)v, 0≤r≤m, are an explicit independent field string basis and their A-span is exactly U_Av by the Gaussian E/F and toral action formulas. Hence this PARTICULAR Z[q±] lattice is free without the held general global-freeness theorem. Use the local character comparison only for the general field-level conclusion. The integral generator family includes every E^(r),F^(r), not merely E,F; its explicit rank-one divided action has Gaussian coefficients in A, so it preserves the free lattice spanned by F^(t)v. Conversely each of these basis vectors is an integral divided generator applied to the highest vector, proving equality with U_Av. For m=2, the smaller ordinary-generator algebra would generate only A v_0+A v_1+A[2]v_2, with [2] a nonunit; this explains why the displayed generator correction is essential.

items.title: Direct substitution $q=1$ into quantum rational expressions is not the specialization
items.statement:
**Statement refuted.** Let $M$ be a weight module with a $U_A$-stable lattice and $\bar M$ its specialization at $q\mapsto1$. Then the operator induced by an element $x\in U_A$ is computed by substituting $q=1$ into any expression of $x$ as a rational function of $q$ with coefficients in $U_A$, numerator and denominator specializing separately.

**Counterexample.** In the rank-one quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ take $x=[K;0]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}=T_{0,1}\in U_A$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). The numerator $K-K^{-1}$ and the denominator $q-q^{-1}$ both vanish under the substitution $K\mapsto1$, $q\mapsto1$, so the naive rule gives the undefined symbol $0/0$. The actual specialization is the coroot label: on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the operator $x$ acts by $[\mu(h)]_q\mapsto\mu(h)$, which is generally nonzero ([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]](ii)). Concretely, on the two-dimensional module $L(1)$ with $K=\mathrm{diag}(q,q^{-1})$ and basis $v_0,v_1$, $x$ acts as $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$, whereas substituting $q=1$ into $K$ gives the identity operator: the naive substitution loses the entire Cartan action. The same failure occurs for the divided-power commutation coefficients $\frac{1}{q^b-q^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1})$ of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](ii), whose denominator vanishes at $q=1$ while the operator specializes to the finite value given by the string formula, and for the Gaussian-binomial expression $[m]_q=\frac{q^m-q^{-m}}{q-q^{-1}}$, whose naive value at $q=1$ is again $0/0$ although the correct specialization is the integer $m$. The repair is the integral-form statement of [[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]]: specialization is defined on elements of $U_A$ (and on lattice operators), not by substituting into rational expressions.
items.strategy:
Step 1 (the element and its two evaluations). $x=T_{0,1}\in U_A$ is a generator of the integral form; on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ it acts by the scalar $[\mu(d_ih_i)]_{q_i}=[\mu(h_i)]_i$, which at $q\mapsto1$ is the integer $\mu(h_i)$. The naive substitution $K\mapsto1$, $q\mapsto1$ into $(K-K^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ is $0/0$: both $K-K^{-1}$ and $q-q^{-1}$ specialize to $0$, and no value is defined by separate substitution. This refutes the displayed general principle.

Step 2 (explicit witness). In the two-dimensional module of [[ex-quantum-verma-and-simple-modules-for-sl-two]] with $m=1$, $K$ acts as $\mathrm{diag}(q,q^{-1})$ and $x=T_{0,1}$ as $\mathrm{diag}([1]_q,[-1]_q)=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$; the specialization of $x$ is $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$, a nonzero operator, while the substitution $q=1$ into $K$ yields the identity. Hence the operator induced by $x$ is not obtained by substituting $q=1$ into the expression for $x$.

Step 3 (further witnesses). $[m]_q=(q^m-q^{-m})/(q-q^{-1})$: numerator and denominator vanish at $q=1$, while the correct specialization is the polynomial value $m$ ([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]](ii)); the divided-power coefficient $\frac{1}{q^b-q^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q^{-2s}K-q^{2s}K^{-1})$ vanishes in numerator and denominator at $q=1$ yet acts on a weight vector $w$ of weight $\mu$ with $E_iw=0$ by the finite value $[\mu(h_i)-b+1]_i\mapsto\mu(h_i)-b+1$, as the string formula $E_iF_i^{(b)}w=[\mu(h_i)-b+1]_iF_i^{(b-1)}w$ shows by the geometric-sum identity. Each of these is an element of $U_A$ whose value at $q=1$ is defined through the integral form, not through term-by-term substitution.

Step 4 (correct statement). By [[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]], the specialization is the base change $U_A\otimes_Ak$ with $q\mapsto1$, which is well defined because the generators of $U_A$ are actual elements (and the operator matrices on lattice modules are polynomial); the cancellations in Steps 1-3 are handled inside $U_A$. No choice is used.
